actionItems: matthew@linktr.ee: Start the notifications-platform thread and loop in Manny and Lawrence
michael@linktr.ee: Share context on whether push can be supported in the new notification platform and how
matthew@linktr.ee: Clarify the notification/attribution requirements with Weiyang and Lawrence on the data side
decisions: Use the notification platform for recommendation-triggered messages instead of leaning on Braze for this flow
Start with email and in-app notifications; push may stay on Braze for now if needed
Keep the recommendation email simple and templated for now, with no images/fancy creative
Use SES for email sending through the existing SES repo/service rather than Braze
followUps: Notification platform rollout for email, in-app bell/hub, and push support
Brand/design process for recommendation emails and whether new templates are needed
Attribution/click ID approach with Weiyang and Lawrence
keyPoints: Pulse was described as a simplified recommendations system that reviews link/profile content and generates guidance such as fixing dead links or shortening copy.
The goal is for recommendations to fan out into the notification system and open the chat panel on the right side via deep links.
The ideal comms model is channel-agnostic for sending systems: request a notification once, let the platform decide the best channel(s) and fallbacks.
The platform was described as handling opt-outs, frequency caps, bounce suppression, and channel failures safely.
Attribution is important: they discussed generating a notification ID/click ID and attaching it to downstream links/events so actions can be tied back to a specific notification.
They discussed analyzing which channels lead to the most actions and potentially deprioritizing weaker channels later.
Braze was framed as likely staying for some existing uses, but not ideal for this notification flow because it is harder for engineers/agents to work with programmatically.
The new email path is via SES, using templates in the SES repo/service; the repo still has an old SendGrid name.
The current Braze email process was described as very manual, involving PMM, brand creative, consultants, and Stripo before syncing into Braze.
The initial recommendation emails are expected to be simple and templated, with different copy/CTA rather than image-heavy creative.
openQuestions: How push notifications will be supported, if at all, in the new platform
Whether one stable notification/click ID will span all channels or be channel-specific
What the final email template/design process should be if branding becomes more involved
summary.overview: Matthew and Michael aligned on using the notifications platform as the lightweight path for Pulse recommendations: send recommendation-triggered messages via email and in-app hub/bell, deep link back into chat, and track attribution with notification/click IDs. They agreed to keep the first version simple and self-serve, likely using SES for email rather than Braze, while push support and the exact brand/design workflow remain open follow-ups.
